records.assessment: Both original one-line additions were reviewed. Inline crypto passthrough in dm-linear is already represented by the native DM_TARGET_PASSES_CRYPTO feature, and the entire ported dm-linear.c equals LTS. Retain that feature for the added dm-bow target instead of restoring the obsolete per-target may_passthrough_inline_crypto member. The native-style table capability intersection and no-capability-widening checks remain. Local fs_mgr places dm-bow below dm-default-key, providing a positive encrypted-stack consumer. New bow clones use the existing bio_alloc_clone/bio_split helpers: __bio_clone calls bio_crypt_clone, preserving crypto context and the Android skip-default-key marker; split advances the DUN through native bio_advance. This does not assert actual hardware crypto or emulator runtime validation.

Both callback signature changes are retained in dm-bow and dm-default-key: cmd, arg and bool *forward match the native LTS target API. These targets leave forward unchanged, so the native caller initializes and preserves normal forwarding. Keep the return-1 restrictions for a partial backing device (and nonzero default-key start); native dm_blk_ioctl still requires CAP_SYS_RAWIO for that case. No ioctl interception or privilege relaxation is added. The enabled callbacks are compiled by the existing SDK workflow; no ioctl runtime test is claimed.
